capability: Merchant account and store owner (Shopify Account, Store Owner; Salla Your profile / الملف الشخصي, Merchant)
note: The merchant's own account on the platform and the person who owns the store. Shopify holds it mostly in its Terms of Service (Account Terms, Store Owner) and the account's store list; Salla in its profile settings, its Merchant API folder and the store.owner.changed event (M-002). Sign-in security (Shopify SH-C-007, Salla's two-factor and biometric flags) is the TRU batch's.

capability: The merchant agreement's contracting party and governing law (Shopify Contracting Party; Salla's owning company, شركة منصة سلة للاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات / شركة تطبيق سلة لتقنية المعلومات, شركة سلة القابضة)
note: The legal entity of the platform's group that is party to the merchant's agreement, and the law that governs it (M-001). Shopify chooses the entity by the store's billing address; Salla's held statements name its company in partner, app-store, theme-store, affiliate, campaign and migration terms, not in the merchant usage agreement (اتفاقية الاستخدام, SA-C-170), which batch 2 lands.

capability: Several stores under one owner (Shopify Organization and its stores; Salla Manage stores / إدارة المتاجر, قائمة المتاجر المرتبطة)
note: Joined on role (U-009): both group several stores under one owner's account and let the owner move between them. Shopify's organization also carries organization-scoped settings (Users, Billing) that Salla's linked-stores list doesn't show.

capability: Business entity a store operates as (Shopify Business entity: Individual, Company, Non-Profit; Salla الكيان القانوني / نوع الكيان)
note: The registered business or individual behind a store. Shopify keeps business entities in Organization settings and in General; Salla's statements are steps of its store verification (SA-C-006, domain C, names A under also). No shared grouping puts it under another capability, so it has no parent.

capability: Selling with multiple business entities from one store (Shopify Selling with multiple entities)
note: Several business entities, each with its own Shopify Payments account, assigned to markets. Shopify's own route business-entities/:businessEntityId sits under Payments, and its help names the entities of CM-ACC-004.

capability: Store details and general settings (Shopify General, Store properties; Salla General / عام, Settings)
note: The store's own general settings page and its API (M-006): Shopify Settings > General; Salla Settings > General with Store activity and Maintenance mode beneath it.

capability: Maintenance mode (Salla Maintenance mode / وضع صيانة المتجر)
note: Salla gives it its own route under General (general/maintenance-mode) and a plan line. Shopify's statements hold no maintenance or password-page setting (see its cell).

capability: Countries where the platform offers its service (Salla Available in / مدعوم في; Shopify Unsupported countries and regions)
note: Joined on role: Salla states the markets it serves; Shopify states the countries and regions it doesn't support. Shopify's sanctions concern (SH-C-174) and its sign-up location (SH-C-006) are the TRU and ONB batches' to land. Homonym (Q1's U-034, "supported countries"): WooCommerce's WooPayments supported countries (WC-C-010) are the countries of a payment service, not of the platform; the Shopify statements cited here are the platform-wide ones, not Shopify Payments' sanctions clauses (SH-S-0122, SH-S-0131).

capability: Staff accounts: the people other than the owner who work in the store's admin (Shopify Users, Staff Accounts; Salla Staff members, Employees / حسابات الموظفين)
note: Both platforms give it a settings route of its own (Shopify Users; Salla Staff members, /users), a plan line and an API (Shopify read_users, StaffMember; Salla Employees). Grain (M-004): Shopify splits staff accounts (SH-C-009) from roles and permissions (SH-C-010); Salla keeps both in SA-C-009, which lands here as the coarser concern. Its children are roles and permissions, user groups and staff targets, each with a route under this one.

capability: Roles and permissions of staff (Shopify Roles, permissions; Salla Roles & permissions / إدارة الأدوار الوظيفية)
note: Parent CM-STF-001: both platforms route roles under staff accounts (Shopify settings:organizations:accounts:roles; Salla /users/roles). The platform's permission system itself: the permissions each other capability cites are evidence for those capabilities, not here.

capability: User groups: staff grouped to receive roles together (Shopify Custom user groups)
note: Shopify gives it a route (settings:organizations:accounts:groups) and a plan line (Custom user groups, Plus). Parent CM-STF-001 by that route. Salla's statements hold none; Salla's Customer groups are buyers' groups, domain D's (CM-CUS-002), not this.

capability: Staff targets (Salla Employees targets)
note: Salla gives it a route of its own under Staff members (/users/targets). Neither platform's held statements define it: Salla names it only by its link.

capability: Third-party access to the merchant's admin, requested and granted per store (Shopify Collaborator access, collaborators; Salla support access requests / طلبات الدخول للمساعدة)
note: Joined on role (U-010): a partner outside the store's staff requests access to the merchant's admin and the merchant grants and limits it. No parent: Shopify routes it under its users (settings:organizations:accounts:collaborator) and files its permission under USER_MANAGEMENT; Salla routes it under its manage pages (/manage/support-access), beside custom URLs, webhooks and migration, not under /users. The partner's own side (its account, its partner portal) is domain F's.

capability: Subscription plans: the plan a store subscribes to, with its tiers and prices (Shopify Plan: Basic, Grow, Advanced, Plus; Salla Store plan / باقة المتجر: basic, plus, pro, special)
note: What the platform sells the merchant and gates by (M-007). Shopify keeps it in Settings > Plan, the subscribe and pick-period routes, the Plus section and the ShopPlan API object; Salla in Settings > Store plan (/plan) and its plans flag. What each plan includes is part of this capability: each plan line or plan-scoped flag is evidence for the capability it names, in that capability's domain, and no platform gives entitlements as such a place apart from the plan (the notes, batch 3). The plan's children here: its term and renewal (CM-PLN-002) and the fee on sales it sets (CM-PLN-003). A free trial and the inactive and pending-termination states are the ONB batch's.

capability: Plan term and renewal: the subscription's billing period, its contract term and its renewal (Shopify Pay monthly / Pay yearly, Shopify Plus Terms, Switch to 3-year term, Renewals; Salla annual subscription / الاشتراك السنوي, automatic renewal / تجديد باقة المتجر تلقائياً)
note: Shopify gives the Plus contract and its renewals a place of their own (plus/renew, plus/terms, the contractmanagement operations, SH-C-201) and the period a route (subscription/pick_period/:plan/:period); Salla states the annual subscription's freeze as a plan line and the plan's automatic renewal from the store balance.

capability: Platform fee on the merchant's sales, set by plan (Shopify Third-party transaction fees; Salla platform commission on sales / عمولة منصة على مبيعاتك)
note: A fee the platform takes on the value of the merchant's sales, varying by plan. Shopify's applies only to orders through payment providers other than Shopify Payments and shows on the bill (settings/billing) as well as in the plan table; both platforms show it as a plan line, so it sits under the plan. Payment processing fees are domain C's.

capability: Platform billing: the platform's charges to the merchant, its bills and invoices (Shopify Billing, Shopify bills; Salla Balance & billing / الرصيد والفواتير, إعدادات الفوترة)
note: How the platform bills the merchant (M-008): the billing section, the list of charges and invoices, the billing currency, and who may see them. App charges billed through the platform are domain F's (CM-APP-003); partner billing is F's (CM-PTN-004).

capability: Paying the platform's bills: the means the platform charges for its fees (Shopify billing payment methods, Authorized Payment Method, Pay bills; Salla the store balance that renews the plan, iTunes balance in Salla's iOS app / رصيد آيتونز)
note: Joined on role (reading): what the merchant's bills are paid from. Shopify charges a payment method the merchant keeps on file; Salla draws on the prepaid store balance (CM-PLN-006), and its سلة بلس plan line lets the subscription be managed in its iOS app with iTunes balance.

capability: Prepaid store balance with the platform: topped up, spent on the platform's services and withdrawn (Salla Store balance / رصيد المتجر, Wallet / محفظة المتجر)
note: Salla's balance, held apart from the e-payments balance (SA-S-0091), which is domain C's. Salla's own plan-feature grouping puts it with billing (the heading محفظة المتجر والفوترة, SA-I-1061), and Settings links Balance & billing as one page. Homonym: Shopify Balance (SH-C-088, domain C) is a money account for the merchant's sales, not a balance that pays Shopify.

capability: Taxes on the platform's own charges (Shopify Taxes on Shopify bills, Tax registration; Salla VAT on Salla's fees / ضريبة القيمة المضافة على إجمالي الرسوم)
note: Tax the platform adds to what it charges the merchant, not the merchant's sales tax (domain C). Q1's M-009 joins Shopify's SH-C-017 with WooCommerce's WC-C-057; Salla's statement sits in SA-C-113, domain C (U-029).

capability: Merchant's country at sign-up: the location the merchant gives when creating the store (Shopify I'm located in:, Country/region; Salla store country / دولة المتجر)
note: The country or region the merchant states on the sign-up or registration step. Shopify asks it on its sign-up page and requires the location to be kept current in the admin; Salla asks the store's country at registration, and says it decides the government documents the store is set up with. Joined on role (reading). Apart from CM-ACC-008, the countries where the platform offers its service: this is the one merchant's own location. Salla's SA-S-0141 is cited in both (see the notes, batch 4).

capability: Store status in its lifecycle: restricted access, suspension, inactivity, pending termination, reactivation and closure (Shopify store-unavailable, restricted access, inactive-account, pending-termination, reactivation, Term and Termination; Salla suspension of the store / إيقاف متجرك)
note: The states a store passes through when the platform restricts, suspends or terminates it or the merchant closes it, and the way back. Shopify places them in admin routes of their own (store-unavailable, inactive-account, pending-termination, reactivation) and in its Terms; Salla's held statement is only its violations page's warning that an uncorrected violation suspends the store. The violations and acceptable-use enforcement themselves are the TRU batch's (SH-C-172, SA-C-232). Homonym: domain G's CM-OPS-004 "Store status" is WooCommerce's system status report, not a store's lifecycle state.

capability: The platform's support and learning for merchants (Shopify 24/7 support, Shopify Academy, Shopify Learn, Shopify Community; Salla Help Center / مركز المساعدة - سلة, support plan, dedicated account manager / مدير حساب مخصص)
note: The help the platform's company gives its merchants: support by chat or an account manager, a help centre, courses and a community. Q1's M-066. Its level is set by plan on both (Shopify's 24/7 support row; Salla's سلة سبيشل lines). Homonym: SA-C-014's name carries "Self-service system", but Salla's Self-service system (نظام التذاكر) is the merchant's ticket system for its own customers, domain D's CM-SUP-005; no SA-C-014 statement holds it. Salla's support team's temporary access requests (SA-S-5132) are cited in CM-STF-005.

capability: Sign-in security for the admin: two-step authentication, passkeys and the sign-in methods of the platform's accounts (Shopify Security, two-step authentication, Sign in with passkey, External login services; Salla two-factor authentication / المصادقة الثنائية, نظام التحقق بخطوتين)
note: How the platform secures sign-in to the store's admin: a second step at sign-in, passkeys, sign-in with outside accounts, and for Shopify organizations MFA management, SAML and SCIM. Shopify places it in Settings > Security and the organization's accounts:security route; Salla states two-factor sign-in to its dashboard as mandatory (a help heading of SA-C-234, domain G with A under also) and holds two unreleased flags in its profile concern (SA-C-001). Joined on role (Q1's U-006: two-step against two-factor). No parent: Shopify's route sits under the organization's accounts (all users, not the owner's account alone) and Salla's two-step heading under platform security, so neither grouping puts it under CM-ACC-001 (reading). The buyers' sign-in is domain D's (CM-CUS-010 to CM-CUS-013).

capability: Identity verification of the people behind a store (Shopify Identity verification, Trust, Profile Assessment; Salla the store owner's identity checked through Absher / أبشر, and beneficial owners' data, in store verification)
note: The platform checks the identity of the store owner and of the people who own or run the business. Shopify gives it a route and admin sections of its own (profile-assessment, Trust, ProfileAssessment); Salla's held statements check the owner's identity and ask beneficial owners' data only as steps of its store verification (SA-C-006, domain C with A under also; the same statements are held under SA-C-232). Joined on role (Q1's U-007). The verification of the store's legal entity for payments, Shopify Payments' KYC (SH-C-068) and Salla's Store Verification, is domain C's.

capability: Audit log of admin activity (Shopify Merchant audit log, activity log, audit_events/admin_api_activity; Salla Activity history / سجل العمليات, audit_logs_management)
note: A record of the actions taken in the store's admin, by staff and through the API, for the merchant to review (Q1's M-005). Salla's Logs section (/logs) also holds the export log, which is domain G's CM-MIG-004. Homonym (Q1's U-044, "log"): WooCommerce's and BigCommerce's store logs, the entries a logger records, are domain G's CM-OPS-005, not this.

capability: Bot protection at checkout (Shopify Bot protection, CommerceProtection)
note: Shopify only so far: blocking known bots from the checkout and slowing bot activity, on Shopify Plus. Not reCAPTCHA at buyers' sign-in and registration, domain D's CM-CUS-012, nor API rate limits, domain F's (Q1's U-045: "rate limit" names an API limit on Shopify and Salla).

capability: Customers' personal data in the store: privacy settings, consent, data requests and erasure (Shopify Customer privacy, Privacy, Request data, Erase personal data; Salla customers' personal data under نظام حماية البيانات الشخصية, website-cookies, customer-data-export, customer-account-deletion)
note: Q1's M-059 at its coarser grain: Salla keeps cookies, data export and deletion in one concern (SA-C-066), Shopify splits privacy settings and consent (SH-C-148, CM-TRU-006) from data requests and erasure (SH-C-149, CM-TRU-007). This parent holds what the platforms state of the merchant's privacy duties as a whole. The data-protection roles (controller, processor: Shopify SH-C-180, Salla SA-C-171, Q1's M-060) are the next batches'. The store's privacy policy page is domain E's CM-CNT-008; the privacy compliance webhooks to apps domain F's CM-API-011.

capability: Privacy settings and cookie consent for the store's visitors (Shopify Customer privacy settings, Cookie banner, Customer Privacy API; Salla website-cookies, consent to the store's privacy policy at registration)
note: The store's privacy settings by region, its cookie consent banner, and the API that carries visitors' consent. Shopify places them in Settings > Customer privacy; Salla holds an unreleased flag and the consent notice at buyers' registration. Customers' marketing consent is domain D's CM-CUS-007.

capability: Customer data requests and erasure (Shopify Request data, Erase personal data; Salla customer-data-export, customer-account-deletion)
note: The merchant answers a customer's request for their personal data, or has it erased. Shopify places them as staff permissions in Customers and as access scopes; Salla holds two dashboard flags only, whose subject no statement states. The webhooks that pass these requests to apps are domain F's CM-API-011.

capability: The platform's own use of the store's customer data across merchants for its services, under the merchant's setting (Shopify: Shopify Network Intelligence, Enhanced Services)
note: Shopify only so far: Enhanced Services, powered by Shopify Network Intelligence, which lets Shopify use the store's customers' personal data with other merchants' for its own services, Shopify acting as controller; the merchant may turn the setting off. Its parent is CM-TRU-006 because Shopify places the setting in the Customer privacy settings (SH-S-6326). Salla's analysis of customers' data across its stores for a fraud tag and for cash on delivery (SA-S-5052, SA-S-0110) is a feature's input, cited in its own capabilities; see the notes, batch 5.

capability: Acceptable use and enforcement: the platform's rules on what merchants may do with it, reports of violations and the platform's action on them (Shopify Acceptable Use Policy, Report an issue with a merchant, Resolving terms violations; Salla Violations / المخالفات)
note: The rules the merchant must keep and how the platform enforces them. The store states that follow (restricted access, suspension, termination) are CM-ONB-002. Salla's usage policy (سياسة الاستخدام على منصة سلة, SA-C-170) isn't held as text. The businesses Shopify Payments prohibits are domain C's (SH-C-173).

capability: The merchant's legal compliance as the seller: responsibility for its goods and transactions, and the laws, licences and product rules it must keep (Shopify Your Responsibilities, Compliance, Product disclosures; Salla compliance with e-commerce laws / امتثالاً لقوانين التجارة الإلكترونية, شهادة توثيق التجارة الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-086 (Shopify with WooCommerce's WC-C-027). Shopify makes the merchant the seller, places guidance in its help's Compliance section and gives product disclosures for required warnings; Salla's held statements require the store's customer-service information and the Business platform's e-commerce certificate under its market's laws. Partners' licences are domain F's. Q1's U-039 (Salla's licences, SA-C-231) is batch 7's.
